prompt: Where was the highest air temperature ever recorded on Earth (WMO)?
teaser: Where was the hottest temperature ever recorded?

targets.label: Furnace Creek (Greenland Ranch), Death Valley, California, USA

turnsOut: Furnace Creek in Death Valley, California, 54 m below sea level: 56.7 °C (134 °F) on 10 July 1913. Libya's 58 °C from 1922 held the title until a WMO panel threw it out in 2012.
sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)

prompt: Where was the lowest air temperature ever recorded on Earth (WMO)?
teaser: Where was the coldest temperature ever recorded?
turnsOut: Vostok Station, high on the East Antarctic ice sheet: −89.2 °C (−128.6 °F) on 21 July 1983. Satellites have since found snow surfaces nearby at around −98 °C, but that is the ground, not the air the record is about.
sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)

prompt: Where is the highest average annual rainfall in the WMO's records?
teaser: Where does the most rain fall in a year, on average?
turnsOut: Mawsynram, in the Khasi Hills of north-east India: 11,872 mm a year, averaged over 38 years. The WMO keeps this record by region, and Asia's is the highest. Neighbouring Cherrapunji holds the 12-month record: 26,470 mm from August 1860 to July 1861.
sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)

prompt: Where was the longest dry spell ever recorded, without any measurable rain (WMO)?
teaser: Where did it go longest without rain?
turnsOut: Arica, on the edge of Chile's Atacama Desert: no measurable rain for 172 months, from October 1903 to January 1918. Over 59 years its rainfall averaged 0.76 mm a year, the lowest in South America.
sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)

prompt: Where was the strongest wind gust ever measured, outside a tornado (WMO)?
teaser: Where was the strongest gust of wind ever measured?
turnsOut: Barrow Island, off Western Australia: 113.2 m/s (408 km/h) as Cyclone Olivia passed on 10 April 1996. The WMO only confirmed it in 2010, ending the reign of Mount Washington's 103.3 m/s gust from 1934.
sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)

prompt: Where is the windiest place on Earth near sea level, by average wind speed over a year (International Journal of Climatology)?
teaser: Where is the windiest place near sea level?
authority: Australasian Antarctic Expedition 1911–14, analysed in the International Journal of Climatology
turnsOut: Cape Denison, where Mawson's 1911–14 expedition had its base: the wind averaged about 20 m/s (72 km/h) over a year. The same gales sweep the coast at least 60 km west, to the old French base of Port Martin, so a pin there counts too.
sourceTitle: Parish & Wendler, The katabatic wind regime at Adelie Land, Antarctica (International Journal of Climatology, 1991)

prompt: Where is the highest point above sea level on Earth (joint government survey, 2020)?
teaser: Where is the highest point on Earth?
authority: Governments of Nepal and China (joint survey)
turnsOut: Mount Everest, on the Nepal–China border: 8,848.86 m, Nepal and China announced together on 8 December 2020. Until then Nepal had used 8,848 m, from a 1954 Survey of India, and China 8,844.43 m, the rock without its snow cap.
sourceTitle: 8848.86 metres. That's the height of Mt Everest now (The Kathmandu Post)

prompt: Where is the lowest land on Earth that is not under water or ice?
teaser: Where is the lowest dry land on Earth?

targets.label: The shores of the Dead Sea

turnsOut: The shores of the Dead Sea: on 31 August 2026 the lake stood 441.33 m below sea level. It drops about a metre a year as the Jordan and the Yarmouk are dammed upstream and its water is pumped away; in 1900 it stood at 392 m below.
sourceTitle: Dead Sea level since 1976 (Israel Water Authority, data.gov.il)
licence: Open government data; fact, own wording

prompt: Where is the highest average annual temperature on record, measured from 1960 to 1966 (Meteorological Magazine)?
teaser: Where is the hottest place on average, all year round?
authority: D. E. Pedgley, Meteorological Magazine (UK Met Office), 1967
turnsOut: Dallol, in Ethiopia's Danakil Depression: a prospecting camp's weather station there averaged 41 °C (106 °F) by day and 28 °C (83 °F) by night over 1960–66, hotter on both counts than anywhere in the world tables of the time.
sourceTitle: Air temperature at Dallol, Ethiopia (Meteorological Magazine, September 1967)

prompt: Where did the most rain ever recorded fall in 24 hours (WMO)?
teaser: Where did the most rain ever fall in one day?
turnsOut: Foc-Foc, 2,290 m up on the volcanic island of La Réunion: 1,825 mm in 24 hours on 7–8 January 1966, as Tropical Cyclone Denise passed. The same storm set the 12-hour record too: 1,144 mm.
sourceTitle: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive: records table (31 July 2025)
